utterances.text: And you joined the department of the Ministry of Defence, known as the security and information service, which is better known as SIS; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I think that towards the end of November, I received an order deploying me to the post of an employee of the Security and Information Office of the Republic of Croatia, and my office was supposed to be in Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And within the SIS, you were attached to -- or you worked within a department known as the SIS Split Administration; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the SIS Split Department. It is one of the departments comprising the SIS administration within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And that, too --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And that department, too, like your current place of work, is located within the Lora navy base in Split; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I worked for that department, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you were within the -- within that -- within the SIS from 1996 through -- April 2003; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From December 1996 until the 1st of April, 2003. The SIS changed its title as of 2002, I believe, it was no longer the SIS. It was called the Military Security Agency.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, your position within the SIS was Deputy Chief of the sector for operative analysis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What was the period?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of September 1999 until April 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you were at one particular stage within the SIS reporting to Mr. Mario Tomasovic, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tomasovic was the chief of that department for a certain time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the time-period was when you reported to Mr. Tomasovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was directly answerable to Mr. Tomasovic between September 1999 and late 2000. I stress, directly. Before that, I carried out other tasks, and I had a different superior within the same department. I was not tasked with analysis all that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, during the period 1996 to year 2000 - I'm sorry, 1999 - what branch of the SIS were you working for within the Split -- SIS Split Administration?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SIS Split Department, among other departments, had operational affairs department. Of when I started working for the SIS in Split, that is to say, as of December 1996 until September 1999, I worked in the operational affairs Department of the SIS Split Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, isn't that correct that that section you worked for during that period carried out counter-intelligence work?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SIS works on security and counter-intelligence matters. In terms of security and counter-intelligence, this is the tasks we performed in keeping with the orders of our chain of command and the existing rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, you know, in your statement, you provide quite a number of personal details about where you studied, your previous jobs before you joined the military police department, the type of training you received. Was there any particular reason that you omitted the fact that you served in the SIS for a significant part of your career, from your statement, from your testimony? What was the reason for that omission?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no particular reason. I worked for the SIS as of late 1996 onwards. I think that the period of interest for this case would be period preceding that, when I worked for the military police. I didn't find it necessary to mention this in particular, and such topics were not raised in the course of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milas, isn't that correct that you were, in fact, an operative who participated in the project known as OA Haag; and, in fact, I could tell you the Trial chamber is familiar with that operation?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not an operative working for or as part of the Operative Action Haag or The Hague. I don't know who filed, who initiated the action. I don't know what its aim was. I don't know who its participants were. I don't know who was supposed to be reported to about that action. I'm specifying all the elements which are a must in documents concerning the filing of an operative action. Once it is initiated in the initial or basic document one has to find all these elements. I was never included in anything called Operative Action Haag in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you not involved in concealing documents which were required by the ICTY in relation to the case against General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would absolutely take no part in such a thing if I knew that this Tribunal would seek such documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Milas, that you, in fact, personally participated in receiving documents from the archives in Bosnia, which you were aware of were required by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I never received a single document for which I knew was a document sought by The Hague Tribunal, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could all extra microphones be switched off while the witness is answering, thank you, because of the background noise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, isn't it correct that not only were you -- I'm putting aside the previus question. Weren't you involved in preparing, securing, interviewing, and preparing witnesses for the Blaskic -- the Defence of Blaskic -- General Blaskic in this Tribunal. The preparations took place, in fact, at your department?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never spoke to any of the witnesses who were supposed to be heard by the Tribunal about any details of possible testimony. I did not participate in any way, in anything that would have to do with such witnesses foreseen to testify before this Honourable Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are you saying that did you not participant in any way in securing witnesses for the Blaskic Defence. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You asked me whether I participated in the preparations of witnesses, I did not, concerning the case against General Blaskic. This is something completely different.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you involved in securing witnesses for the Defence of any Croatian indictees in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within a certain period of time, starting with 1997 onwards, we were tasked with providing a room which would be adequately prepared, in which the attorney, Ante Nobilo, with his associates, would proof potential witnesses for the case instituted against General Blaskic in The Hague. That is to say, we had to provide the technical means and characteristics of the room, and we were supposed to be at the service of the team of attorneys. We would have to wait for them at the airport, take them to their hotel, and then from the hotel to the facility where proofing was done. As for the witnesses who were being proofed, we had to provide refreshments and food. As for any choice of witness, documentation, or any type of participation in the course of such proofings, that is something that I was not engaged in. This only included providing security -- technical preconditions for the work of attorney Ante Nobilo and his associates, such as Ms. Slakovic and Mr. Naomovski. This was done so that on the premises of the department, they could proof their witnesses according to the pace determined by them. We did not participate directly in the course of the proofing, and we had nothing to do with the choice of witnesses at the level I worked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, may I take you back to one of your previous answers. When you were asked about preparing, securing, interviewing, and preparing witnesses for the Blaskic case, you said: "I never spoke to any of the witnesses who were supposed to be heard by the Tribunal about any details of possible testimony." Then you continued your answer by saying: "I did not participate in any way, in anything that would have to do with such witnesses foreseen to testify before this Honourable Court." In your last answer you explained to us that you provided a room in your premises, technical facilities which were used by counsel to proof those witnesses. Would you consider this that would you did not participate in any way, in anything, that would have to do with such witnesses foreseen to testify? I would say, I'm inclined to think, that you did participate in the way you described and that that had to do with Blaskic witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours. But not in terms of the subject of their testimony. As I said, I did participant, I was present --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You first denied that. You said you had nothing to do with it. I had nothing to do in any way with -- and now you say -- okay. I just want it remind you that if you would have said in your first answer, I had nothing to do with the subject of their testimony but just we facilitated the proofing, then it would be have been easier for all of us, and we could have moved on more quickly. Can I ask you one additional question. You said technical facilities, would that include recording, tape-recording of the proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In one instances, as far as I can recall, the counsel, Ante Nobilo, requested to be provided with equipment so that he could record those proofing sessions. The employee who worked in Split provided a tape recorder or a cassettophone [as interpreted]. I can't recall what it was so that Counsel Nobilo could use it for his needs. Your Honour, when I said did participate, as I said, in this portion, but I understood the question of the Prosecutor to relate to the subject matter of the -- of the witness testimonies and what they would say before The Hague Tribunal. In that sense, did I not. But certainly, when the technical facility -- where the technical facilities are concerned, yes, I did participate in that aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was the -- were there any recording facilities available in that room apart from the ones Mr. Nobilo had asked for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. As far as I know, no. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you ever had access to the subject matter which was discussed during the proofing sessions, either since it was reported to you or whether -- or by having access to any recording of such proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The topic of discussion of the counsel with the Defence in that room was something that I never knew anything about, nor did I ever discuss this with the witnesses; if I were to meet them, maybe and have a cup of coffee in one of the cafeterias that we had on the premises there. Simply put, I did not know what it was that they discussed because there were three of us who were at the disposal of the counsel, Defence counsel, to assist them with anything that they may need, take or pick up a witness, or drive a witness someplace, take them to the hotel, and so on. But in no way did this have to do with our -- any type of direct knowledge as to what the subject matter of their conversations and discussions was. All I knew was that these were possible witnesses in the proceedings against General Blaskic, and Counsel Nobilo was the Defence counsel for General Blaskic together with his team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, may I have document 7291 , please. That's a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: While the document comes up, Mr. Milas, isn't it correct that you were, in fact, investigated by Croatian authorities, the authorities who investigated into OA Haag regarding your personal involvement in OA Haag and other connected operations which were in place to assist the Defence in the cases relating to Croatian indictees at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And in -- in front of you, on the screen, Mr. Milas, can you see this document. Did you know of the existence of this document? This is a report submitted by two assistant ministers of the Ministry of Interior. And you can see whom the report is addressed to. There's a deputy prime minister, Dr. Granic, minister of the internal affairs; you can read all the addressees there, director of information service, head of office of cooperation with ICTY and others. Now, did you know that this report existed?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this is dated 22nd August 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could just move to page 4, both English and Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 it starts by saying: "This document is an attempt to systematically gather at one place all information and facts, as well as measures and operations undertaken by two police services of the MUP." And, you know, there are several lines there. I will take you right to the point that I want to draw your attention to. That is line 9, which says: "Following the crime activities and influence of the state organs serving in the intelligence community of the Republic of Croatia and other individuals from the Republic of Croatia aimed at explaining or hiding the facts and evidence in relation to Ahmici and in relation to the case against General Blaskic argued before the ICTY, issuing counterfeit IDs to crime perpetrators, measures taken by the MUP aimed to locating them, et cetera." This is a report on the investigations by the Croatian authorities and if we could go, Mr. Registrar, to English version, page 22, and Croatian version, page 21. There's a section titled: "Involvement of the intelligence services of the Republic of Croatia and state and political organs in the investigation of the crime in Ahmici?" If we could just focus on the English version next page. That is English version page 23, but we can remain on the same page, as far as Croatian version goes. I want to draw your attention to the paragraph. It's the top paragraph on the English version. It reads, sir, I'm starting half way: "SIS RH initiated the investigation committed by the Muslims and Serbs against the Croats in BiH. With the purpose to support those crimes with evidence, the documentation and persons prepared for possible important testimonies in the process in The Hague were sent to RH from BiH. For certain persons who came to RH (Lora, i.e., SIS in Split) personal identification documents were going obtained and similar. However, it is obvious as the analysis of the crime in Ahmici was done at the same time so that those documents were also transferred from BiH to RH and were stored in the premises of SIS in Split. Those involved in the realization of those activities were," and I might mispronounce his name, "Udiljak," U-d-i-l-j-a-k, "Ivanovic, Krpan, B. Milas, Mato Zeko, and others." Now the reference there to Ivanovic is to Marin Ivanovic. Isn't that correct, Mr. Milas, the Defence investigator to interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And the person referred to as B. Milas, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean the investigator who spoke with me? Whom are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Marin Ivanovic who interviewed you for this case?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Ivan Marinovic, I beg your pardon. Marin Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, in what context what I did I have this conversation with him about? I don't understand. What did he talk to me about?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, my only question was: The person referred to as Ivanovic in this paragraph is Marin Ivanovic, the Defence investigator to interviewed you; is that correct? Who interviewed you in relation to this case?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And this document is lengthy, but let me take you to the excerpts which is relevant to you. And if you could move on to English page 4 and page 22 of the Croatian version. The first paragraph -- I will start with that sentence: "The objective of the action was to follow the initiated trial" -- I'm sorry, page 24 of the English version. I think you are on that one, and page 22 of the Croatian version, the first paragraph right at the top. "The objective of the action was to follow the initiated trial of General Blaskic. Within OA process, operation action named Haag Put and Istina were organised. The operation actions Put and Istina were under the authority of the Ministry of Defence RH, i.e., SIS whereas the Operative Action Haag was supposed to be under the authority of other state ministries. Firstly, means MUP and Ministry of Justice, but this was not implemented so that the action was still operatively covered by SIS? "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And on that same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hold on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: On the same page, we have a section entitled manipulation with the documentation of the HVO. I think on the Croatian version it's the next page. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if you could move to, on the English page, if you could just move to the next page, Mr. Registrar. And on the Croatian version, if you could move to page 23. The portion I want to read on the Croatian version is at page 23, I believe, the next page. I'm sorry, it's already on here. Do you note that paragraph that starts with: "The activities related." It's the last paragraph on the Croatian version. Move on to the next page on the Croatian version. It says: "The activities related to the usage of HVO documentation was intensified within the collection of evidence for the trial in The Hague and Defence of Blaskic but also evidence on defence of the Croats in BiH, i.e., crimes committed by the Muslims and Serbs in BiH against the Croats. For that reason, but also for the fear that HVO documentation would end up in possession of SFOR," and there is an footnote there that says, "the media announced that SFOR in BiH is looking for the documentation. The decision was made to withdraw security-important documentation from BiH. That part of the job was done by SIS in Split so that on several occasions four vans of material was brought and stored in the premises of SIS in Split (in the barracks Lora on the second floor rooms, 73, 74, 75 and 76) under the order of Markica Rebic and Ante Gugic. The operative covering and storing of the documents was done by the members of SIS Split (Mario Tomasovic, Bosko Ramljak, Boris Milas, Palac Predrag, Klapiric Boris, Boris Boban)." Now, Mr. Milas, this official report compiled on the investigation into OA Haag, according to which you had been involved, you were one of the operatives, was involved in concealing documents relating to General Blaskic's case. You just denied it when I asked you that question. Do you want to reconsider your answer?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, on the 5th of June 2000 at the summons of the SIS administration, I reported to Zagreb together with Mario Tomasovic and Bosko Ramljak; when we arrived in Zagreb we were told that we would each be assigned, individually, to a room so that I was sent to a room. And in that room there was an employee of the Ministry of Interior and an official of the SIS who were supposed to interview me. They told me and asked me, one, whether I knew what OA Haag was, what OA Put was, what OA Istina was, and I think they also mentioned another OA, Sigma or something like that. I'm not quite sure. I replied that I did not know what these operative actions were and who or why was conducting them. Then they asked me to right down a report and everything I know about the events in Ahmici, the possible perpetrators of those crimes, potential witnesses who could testify to those crime, and also questions relating to documents from Bosnia and Herzegovina, which had been brought from Bosnia to Split. I stayed in that office for about two hours. I wrote a statement about these matters and signed it. I noted, in the statement, that I was, indeed, pursuant to an instruction from the chief of my department in Split, take the actions that we were discussing earlier; namely, providing technical facilities for the Defence counsel and to assist him with proofing the witnesses, and I also wrote about how and in what part -- what my participation was in escorting this train car to the Lora base, this transport of documents, and I also told them how and where I met the person that they asked me about. The name of that person was Ante Sliskovic. So this was a written statement I penned myself. I believe it was three pages, and it was my statement about the circumstances that they were inquiring about. As for the documents, I told them that I did escort this transport of documents to the Lora naval base, that we then unloaded this truck with the documents. All of the documents were in sealed large box so that at no time did I have any insight as to what type of documents they involved, unless there was a note on the box itself, stating, for instance, the 2nd HVO Brigade, transport documents or the 2nd HVO Brigade finances. So that was the extent of my role, and I explained that to the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: But when I asked you, Mr. Milas, as to whether you had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the appropriate time. Mr. President, I need to be heard on ... I said at the appropriate time, I need to be heard on the propriety of the Prosecution's use of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do that before the next break. Would that be an appropriate moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I may proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed at this moment. If you would -- let's see, let's have a break at -- in ten minutes from now. How much time would you need, Mr. Misetic? Five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: These things tend to spiral, so I will say I will try to keep it to three minutes, but I suspect the Prosecution will wish to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed for another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could move to page 27, both English and Croatian version, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now I questioned you about preparation of witnesses, Mr. Milas, and this report also contains a report on that. There is heading titled preparation of witnesses for the testimony in The Hague on Ahmici. And if we could go to paragraph 2, which starts with in: "In September. It reads: "In accepted 1997 SIS Administration ordered that SIS Split would secure technical conditions for the preparation of witnesses for the attorney team of Ante Nobilo" --

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't see that portion of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me read that portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time, Ms. Mahindaratne, you said it was on page 27 of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Croatian, I think you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's correct Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's -- I'll check whether.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think Croatian version starts at the bottom and goes on the -- the Croatian version still on page 24, is it? Croatian version should be on page 27.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's 25 going to -- 25 perhaps, Mr. Registrar. I may have made a mistake. If I could have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem always is, Ms. Mahindaratne, whether you are talking about e-court pages or whether you're talking about the pages appearing in the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: We are on the correct page, Mr. President. It's just that the Croatian version starting from the bottom continues to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's page 25 in e-court, page 24 of the page at the bottom, and I think we have it now on our screen. Could you read the last two lines of this page and then we'll move to e-court page 26, hard copy page 25. You have seen it? Could we move to the next page. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I was at the point: "Preparations for witnesses for the attorney team of and Ante Nobilo and which would be used during the defence of Tihomir Blaskic in The Hague. The preparation of the first crew of witnesses was initiated by the attorney team A. Nobilo in October 1997 and later, besides the attorney team of Nobilo, the preparation of the witnesses for The Hague in SIS Department Split was conducted by the lawyers Naomovski (for Dario Kordic) Goran Mikulicic Jadranka Slakovic-Glumac Misetic and person who lawyers Rasel Hayman and Turner Smith."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You read -- I see that the name Mr. Mikulicic is appearing wrongly in the English translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: "The final preparation of the witnesses in SIS Split, according to available information, was conducted in January 2000, according to the available information from October 1997 to January 2000, there were in total 13 preparations, including around 330 witnesses and the total preparation lasted around 80 days." And on the same page in the English version if you go a few lines down the last line starts from: "From SIS department Split, Mario Tomasovic" -- And in English version next page. "...and Boris Milas were closely cooperating with Zeko and Udiljak in regard to organisation of the affairs." So, in fact, Mr. Milas, when you said that you had no involvement whatsoever in concealing documentation or in preparing witnesses, you were not stating the truth, were you, this is an official documentation, official report into the investigation which identifies you as having been fully involved in the operation, preparing witnesses and concealing document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Judge, I don't believe the report says fully involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, if you would have phrased the question by describing a level of involvement, which apparently you consider to be in contradiction with what the witness said, that would have avoided the objection. Could you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, you were involved to some level in the preparation of witnesses and concealing documents relating to the case against General Blaskic, were you not, contrary to what you stated previously?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "in preparing witnesses," then, yes, in the sense of ensuring technical facilities. And when you speak of "concealing documentation," then I can say that I participated in transport of documents to the Lora Barracks without knowing what documents this involved, in terms of their content, or without knowing that they were being concealed for the purposes of trial, no, I did not participate in that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, we'll soon have a break. I would like to give an opportunity to Mr. Misetic to address the Court in the absence of the witness. Would this be a suitable moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I also wish to inform Court that I intend to tendered this document, but perhaps Court will want to hear Mr. Misetic first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Milas, we'll have a break. Can't tell you how long that will take because procedural issues sometimes take their time. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Milas out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will object to the admission of this document into evidence. The Chamber should be aware of the inconsistent position being taken by Prosecution now. The Blaskic case -- in the Blaskic case, the Prosecution sought a revision of the appeals judgement which was -- and in that motion for reconsideration of the appeals judgement, was decided by the Appeals Chamber on the 23rd of November 2006. The document is titled decision on Prosecutor's request for review or reconsideration. The basis to review the Appeals Chamber judgement is that the Republic of Croatia committed a fraud on the Appeals Chamber with this document that they are now tendering before this Chamber. The allegation was that the Appeals Chamber in its initial judgement received a redacted version of this report, and I call the Chamber's attention specifically to paragraphs 54 going forward. The Prosecution took the position before the Appeals Chamber that had this document been revealed to the Appeals Chamber, in its original form, then the Appeals Chamber would have realized that the source of much of this information is Ante Nobilo, himself. Ms. Mahindaratne now puts it as, This is an official Croatian report and an official investigation, et cetera. When, in fact, if you review what the Prosecution told the Appeals Chamber about the reliability and credibility of this document in light of the fact that Ante Nobilo is the source of this information, then I will quote, for example in paragraph 57 -- and by the way, the Prosecution deemed the initial 20- page version of this report that was a basis of the appeals judgement as a forgery on the basis that Ante Nobilo, as the source of the document, was concealed from the Tribunal. At page 57, the Prosecution took the position that because of the new fact that Mr. Nobilo is, in fact, the source of this report "this report -- this MUP report is not persuasive or reliable because and Nobilo was a source for some of the information in the report." It goes on. At paragraph 60, the second paragraph, the Prosecution told the Appeals Chamber that because Mr. Nobilo's assertions were not corroborated by the underlying evidence for the allegations made in the report, with respect, unless the underlying evidence is brought forward, and this is now in italics in the Appeals Chamber's decision, "this report of is little evidentiary value." Now for the Prosecution to take the position that the entire Blaskic appeals judgement needed to be reversed or at least the portions that referenced the initial 20-page MUP report on the basis this is, to a great extent, Ante Nobilo's vies after Mr. Blaskic was convicted, I might add, by the Trial Chamber, that Mr. Nobilo, as the source of this document, was concealed from both Prosecution and Appeals Chamber and that the Appeals Chamber known that Ante Nobilo is the source of this document, that it would have little evidentiary value and that it is not persuasive or reliable. Your Honours, it is our position that on that basis the Prosecution cannot now tender this as a reliable document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I say that what Mr. Misetic said does not affect the admissibility of this document. In fact, I confronted the witness who is -- who has been privy to these matters who would knew as to what has gone on, the contents. And as to his responses would indicate to the Trial Chamber as to whether there is any reliability in what is reported in this document or not. Further, may I add, Mr. President, that I have a couple of more documents to be tendered into relation to this matter which would demonstrate to the Trial Chamber that there are different sources supporting the contents in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If that is the case, then, when did the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if in fact now Ms. Mahindaratne is saying that, first of all, the document stands on its own; but second of all, I'm perplexed as to how, on the one hand when Mr. Blaskic is an issue, it is unreliable document that's not corroborated by other evidence. And in this case, it is a reliable document that is corroborated by other evidence. The Prosecution is not allowed to take inconsistent position like this in different case. And I would again submit, Your Honours, that the Prosecution should take a position. If this is a reliable document then they should take that position vis-a-vis Blaskic and say that, in fact, it was reliable; or it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President I don't think the Prosecution has to argue about the positions taken in Blaskic. It is not relevant to the proceedings before this Chamber. The -- and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I please invite everyone to refrain from laughing or any other inappropriate behaviour. I expect no party to laugh in relation to the other parties' argument. Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Further, portions of this document was put to the witness and he responded, confirming to an extent what was reported there. And as I said, the document is before the Trial Chamber. There will be other documentation which will be tendered in the course of the next few minutes which will, you know, based on which the Trial Chamber can decide on the reliability of the -- this is an official document that has been sent to us pursuant to RFAs, as far as the OTP is concerned, you know, that is a good basis to -- for admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a standard. The OTP has to speak with one voice. That's a principle. They can not take the position again in one case that it is unreliable document and in another case that it is a reliability document. That is the first point. The second point is - with all due respect to my colleague - what she thinks is going to corroborate what is in this report is yet to be seen, is the first point -- or the second appointment. The third point is: I'm not sure what exactly it is that she thinks was impeached. The witness did not state that he participated in any other manner in terms of -- in preparing witnesses other than what he testified. So if it's a case of Mr. Nobilo versus the witness, then that should be put directly as what it is. If it's something else, then that should be the case. But what I object to is taking a report which the Prosecution itself says is nothing more than Mr. Nobilo speaking. And then classifying it and putting it to the witness as, This is the official Croatian government report or result of an investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it's an official report or not, official reports sometimes do contain information which is not fully or only very partially correct which, of course, is not in itself a reason not to seek to verify what is and what may not be correct. Ms. Mahindaratne, perhaps that would be an emphasis on the report being official. I have seen in my life perfect official reports and official reports which had not yet one per cent truth in it. So, therefore, to emphasise that it's an official report might not add much. Whether or not the Chamber will admit this document finally in evidence is a matter we'll consider at a later stage, once it has been tendered. The Chamber, in consultation with my colleagues, came already to the conclusion that it should be MFI'd to start with, then later see what other evidence comes, whether it has any impact on our decision on relevance or probative value. We'll now first have a break. Mr. Misetic, your primary objection was that it this document should not be admitted into evidence. We, as I said, we will first MFI it. We've heard some of your concerns; we've heard some of the answers of Ms. Mahindaratne. We'll have a break and resume at five minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I could not tender the previous document into evidence, Mr. President. If it could be marked for identification. That is 65 ter 7291.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You announced already that you would tender it. You're tendering it and we have heard already of the objections and as the Chamber indicated before, it will be MFI'd. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2547, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, we noted the date of that previous document, which was August 2000. A few months prior to that, you were interviewed by the Croatian authorities, to be specific in June 2000; isn't that correct? Mr. Milas, you are not responding. Are you receiving the translation or ...

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only received the beginning of what you said, not everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question was: Were you not interviewed in June 2000 by Croatian authorities on the issue of your involvement in concealing documents and assisting the Defence in the Blaskic case.

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have just said, on 5th of June 2000, I was in Zagreb. I was summoned to the Ministry of Defence before a SIS investigator, as well as an investigator of the minister of the interior. I gave a statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, I don't mean to be rude. I just wanted a confirmation from you. Thank you. Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me just state that it was asked an answered page 59, line 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Misetic. Mr. Registrar, can I have 7292, please, that's a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And while that document is coming up, Mr. Milas, weren't you also interviewed again in 2005 by Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2005, if, indeed, it was 2005, I think it was on the premises of the police -- police administration of Split and Dalmatia. I received a summons which was served on me by the military police to report to the police administration at a given time, and it also said that it had to do with the -- with a crime, and it was my interpretation that it had to do with a war crime. No further explanation was given. I was called for an interview at the Split-Dalmatia police administration. I, indeed, was interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, I would be grateful if you could confine your responses to my question because you're running out of time. On the screen you see an official record of interview, and than is the record of interview by yourself taken by the investigator, Mr. Juranic [phoen], isn't that correct, in June 2000?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an Official Note drafted based on the interview with me and based on my written statement. I believe it was done in the offices of the MUP. I can't see who signed it, but I presume it was the MUP employee who interviewed me on the 5th of June, 2005 in the Ministry of Defence building. He drafted his Official Note the way he interpreted our interview and my written statement I gave on the 5th of June, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could you move to an English version, page 4 and the Croatian version, page 3. And on the English version if you could just focus on paragraph 3 and Croatian version also the same paragraph, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is what is recorded by the investigator based on the interview and your statement, Mr. Milas, and I will just read this paragraph. "He remembers that at the end of April or beginning of May 1998, someone from SIS Administration - he is not certain, but thinks that was the chief, or then already deputy minister for intelligence/security affair, Mr. Ante Gugic - called his chief, Mr. Mario Tomasovic, at which time his department received an assignment to receive documentation from the Republic of Herceg-Bosna, which would be brought to them at the department in Split in Furgone trucks across the Vinjani Donji border crossing. None of them, even the chief, knew what kind of documentation this was. And then further next paragraph, line 6: "Upon arriving in Split, they offloaded the contents of trucks which comprised of cardboard boxes and black nylon bags full of documentation and placed this on the second floor in room number 73. Only Chief Tomasovic had the keys to that room. He again reminded that he did not know the contents of the documentation they offloaded from the trucks." And then the last paragraph on the English version: "About one month after the first-above shipment of documentation, 25th June, 1998, to be precise, someone from SIS Administration called Chief Tomasovic just like the first time, and ordered him to again receive documentation from the Republic of Herceg-Bosna, which would be driven to RH in three Furgone trucks across the Vinjani Donji border crossing." And the next paragraph, starting from line five: "Upon arriving in Split, they offloaded the contents of the above trucks which consisted of cardboard boxes, nylon bags, and a couple of wooden crates full of documentation and placed all of the above in rooms numbered 74, 75, and 76, which they locked and stored the keys in the chief's safe. The documentation sat in the rooms for nearly two years and nobody entered the rooms during that time nor did they receive an order from SIS Administration regarding the above documentation." Now, in fact, Mr. Milas, based on your own information given to the investigator, you have ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You have received and participated in storing -- two consignments of documentation. Now, this is your own information which is quite consistent with what I read to you from the previous report. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I'm not sure what is -- what exactly is being put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What the witness has already testified about so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Mahindaratne, please put your next question to the witness. It's clear from what was read that it was at two occasions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me just read one more paragraph to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page, Mr. Registrar. If you could focus on paragraph 2 of the next page, actually, paragraph 1, the sixth line.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: This is your information, Mr. Milas: "In his upon the contents of the documentation that Mr. Anto Damjanovic separated with the help of his associates could help Mr. Ante Nobilo in the appeal process for the conviction of General Tihomir Blaskic." This is regarding what you have stated: "In this response to the specially posed question of what he thinks is the reason the above documentation was taken from BiH and stored with them in the department, Milas stated that he thinks that documentation was pulled out of ABiH at the time when SFOR raided the military and state institutions of Herceg-Bosna and confiscated concern documentation." Now, in your interview, in that interview, you informed the investigator that you were aware that the documentation could help the Defence in the case of General Blaskic, which is what was recorded in this report and that you were aware that they were being brought to Croatia to prevent them getting into the hands of SFOR forces, whereas today when I asked you the question, Mr. Milas, you said you did not know what those documentation were?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I get a page reference as to what she is saying she is impeaching him on. Can we get a transcript reference?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I surprised by this because I think we all remember that when the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What surprises us, it seems that today there are more surprises in both directions than usually. Could you find the -- it corresponds with my memory as well. Let's just verify.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have got that reference, Mr. President. It's page 60, line 3, and let me read that out. "As for the documents I told them that that I did escort this transport of documents to the Lora naval base, that we then under loaded truck with the documents. All of the documents were in sealed large -- so that no time did I have any insight as to what type of documents they involved, unless there was a note on the box itself, stating, for instance, the 2nd HVO Brigade transport documents or the 2nd HVO Brigade finance. That was the extent of my role. I explained that to the investigator." And further up, there was a reference before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Page 49, Mr. President. Line 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now that is exactly my point. The question at page 24 is concealing documents from the ICTY. The question posed is documents that will help General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, from the answer you gave earlier and which was read to you by Ms. Mahindaratne, that was page 60, line 3, one could gain the impression that, where you explained they were in sealed large boxes, or box, and that at no time did you have any insight as to what type of documents they involved, you could gain the impression that you wanted to say that you had no idea about what these documents could serve for. Whereas, in the Official Note, it gives the impression that you formed an opinion as to whether these documents could play a role in the proceedings which suggests that, at least there's some understanding, if not of the content, at least of the role these documents could play. Now, could you explain to us which of the two impressions is the best?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the first one, definitely. The first sentence of the page that have I on the screen, where it says: "In his opinion, the contents of the documentation that Mr. Anto Damjanovic separated with the help of his associates, could help, Mr. Ante Nobilo in the appeal proceedings for the conviction of General Tihomir Blaskic." I never said that. Simply put, I was not familiar with the contents of the documentation. When Anto Damjanovic was there alongside another SIS employee, and when we helped them to take out one, two, or three boxes, which they took to Zagreb, even at that point in time, I did not know what documentation they separated, since they did so independently on the second floor. They were in one of the buildings containing the documentation. They were there alone. No one was present from the SIS Split when they were separating the documentation. All that was pursuant to the authorisation given to them by the then intelligence and security assistant to the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're going into details which are not of direct relevance for the question. What you say is what is said here as to whether you have any idea as to what the separated documents could be helpful for, that Mr. Juranic did not write down your words accurately. This is not what you said. There was a -- yes, that's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There was a second portion of the question which was whether you had awareness or that you understood that the reason for the transfer of these documents was that there existed a fear that they would be searched and seized by SFOR.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I said then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And if you could go back to page 2 of the English version, Mr. Registrar, and in the Croatian version that would also be the same page, I believe, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And there the fourth paragraph onwards, you described your involvement in preparation of witnesses for the case of General Blaskic at the ICTY. And due to lack of time, I'll just go to the last paragraph. You go on to say: "The preparation of the first group of witnesses was begun by the legal team of Mr. Nobilo in October 1997, and later, besides the legal team of Mr. Nobilo, counsellor Mr. Naomovski, who led the defence of Mr. Dario Kordic also conducted the preparation of witnesses for The Hague in their department." Referring to your department. "Besides Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Naomovski, counsels, Mr. Goran Mikulicic and Mrs. Jadranka Slakovic-Glumac, counsellor Mr. Misetic, and American attorneys, Mr. Russel Hayman and Mr. Turner Smith participated in the preparation of witnesses. The last preparation of a witness by Mr. Naomovski was conducted in their department in the month of January 2000. By his assessment" -- and that's your assessment. Mr. Milas was recorded here, "From October 1997 to January 2000, a total of 13 preparations were conducted which encompassed about 330 witnesses and the total preparations lasted about 80 days." Now, this is information read to you from the previous report. When I asked you about your involvement in preparation of witnesses, you mentioned names of two counsels, Mr. Naomovski and another person, but you never mentioned Mr. Misetic's name or Mr. Mikulicic's name; whereas based on this information, you have worked with them on the Blaskic case. Now what was the reason why you omitted to mention Mr. Misetic to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that I did not worked on the Blaskic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that does not appear from this document, as such, is it, Ms. Mahindaratne?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Milas, have you worked with Mr. Misetic before?

utterances.speaker: BORIS MILAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At the time that you were providing --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know, did the transport record his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your answer was? Could you please repeat your answer whether you worked with Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the question please repeated to me. I am afraid I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you worked before with Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never worked with neither of these attorneys in the sense that we discussed something that would have to do with their work as attorneys, with not a single one of them. Usually it was Mr. Nobilo who was there, and I have already said that. I did not work with any of the attorneys or witnesses in direct terms. I did not participate in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, have you had any form of association with Mr. Misetic or Mr. Mikulicic going back to the time before you were interviewed for this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection. Clarify what any form of association.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- Mr. Milas, what is described in the paragraph that was just read to you, does that reflect what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could we go through the persons mentioned there, one by one. We have already -- you've already explained about Mr. Nobilo, Mr. Naomovski. It reads that he led the Defence of Dario Kordic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot assert that I said that Mr. Naomovski was Dario Kordic's counsel. We usually received a notification from the SIS administration stating that this and that attorney at that time would proof this and that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so Mr. Naomovski did his proofing sessions on the premises of the SIS; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I move on to the other persons that are mentioned. Mr. Mikulicic and Mrs. Jandranka Slakovic-Glumac. Did they proof witnesses on the premises of the SIS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For any of the attorneys mentioned, it was stated in the request of the administration that they would undertake proofing sessions. As for whether all of them were present, I don't know. I can confirm that it was true for Ms. Jadranka Slakovic-Glumac around as for Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, are you aware in what capacity, that means counsel, in what case they prepared their witnesses at your premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it had to do with the proceedings against the Vitez group. The persons who, in October 1997, voluntarily surrendered to The Hague Tribunal. I think this is what it had to do with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then next one, Mr. Misetic, he goes without a first name, but that is Mr. Misetic who examined you. But let's just verify, so there is no confusion about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I met Mr. Misetic in 2007. As for whether he was, indeed, was in the SIS department in Split, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say -- you say that this reflects what you said at the time. There could be another Mr. Misetic. I'm not aware of that. Could you confirm or would you deny that the Mr. Misetic mentioned in your statement is Mr. Misetic who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina's Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, I can neither confirm nor deny that. We received notification from the SIS administration that Mr. Misetic would arrive. Whether this is the Mr. Misetic, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an answer to my question. You can confirm nor deny. That's clear. You can do either. As far as Mr. Mikulicic is concerned, Mr. Mikulicic as you may be aware is counsel for Mr. Markac. Can you confirm or deny that - and here we have a first name - that is the same Mr. Mikulicic or can't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In physical terms, I did see Mr. Mikulicic later on when the -- these proceedings began. I knew Mr. Nobilo and Ms. Slakovic, they were the person who visited the most frequently, and they would stay there for eight or nine days at a time. During their breaks, we would have a cup of coffee together --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just keep focussed on the question. Do you physically recognize the Mr. Mikulicic you have seen at that time, if you saw him, with the Mr. Mikulicic who is in court today? Yes, it's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember. I didn't see all the attorneys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then -- no, I didn't ask you about all the attorneys, I asked you about Mr. Mikulicic. But you say you don't remember. Now, as far as Mr. Russell Hayman and Mr. Turner Smith are concerned, have you any recollection as to in what capacity they were there? I mean, counsel for whom, if they were counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that they were members of Mr. Nobilo's team. They worked on those sessions together with him. As for whether they are attorneys or counsel, I don't know. But when Mr. Nobilo was there, they were there own several occasions. I don't know them personally. I know of them in terms of the notifications we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just got names of persons who would appear. You have seen some of them. That was all. And you took care of the technical facilitates. Is the number I just seek clarification of that, 330 witnesses in 80 day; is that correct? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That reflects accurately what I can remember. There were shifts or periods when such sessions would occur, covering a total of 80 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you said earlier that you provided a room, and from what I understood from your testimony, it was at the request of Mr. Nobilo that you provided the room. 330 witnesses in 80 days means four witnesses a day. Was there one room available or did you provide more than one room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the SIS administration, we were tasked with securing a room for Mr. Nobilo's needs. It wasn't someone from Mr. Nobilo's team who addressed us directly. We provided a room, like a half of this courtroom, and there was only one such room where witnesses would be taken in. There was only one room, not several rooms in the department simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there more witnesses in one room when being proofed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say. While the witnesses were waiting, Mr. Nobilo would call in one or two witnesses by their names. Therefore, I cannot deny or confirm. He had his own list against which he checked who of the witnesses were present, and then he would say, Person X/Y, let us -- let's go. Whether he, at any point in time, had two witnesses enter the room at the same time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there ever one of your staff members in the room when the witnesses were proofed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Mr. Nobilo asked that we provide means for him to record the interviews for possible subsequent reproduction, there was an employee of the department who, on one or two occasions, set up the equipment, the microphone, and explained to him how it worked. He even assisted him in the process of recording the interviews.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the interviews, never any staff member was in those rooms following the conversations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not any staff members, save for the technician, who used -- who operated the recording device. It is a hi-fi set that he was familiar with and he would then give the tape of the interviews to the attorney, Mr. Nobilo. We did not keep that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he stay in the room during the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether he was present and how long and whether Mr. Nobilo could operate the equipment with his assistant or he was needed at any point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed -- well, I'm saying please proceed, but, Ms. Mahindaratne, there's not much time anymore to proceed. Mr. Milas, I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, not in any way, whether direct or indirect or communicate or exchange notes or whatever with anyone, not to communicate, speak, write, e-mail, whatever it is, with anyone about your testimony either already given or still to be given tomorrow, because we'd like to see you back tomorrow. We adjourn until tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I could not tender the document into evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well we will do that tomorrow then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 25th of June, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of June, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
